The wardens' book is in the vestry chest (clerk's key; the second key was Wend's, laid with him); two hands write in it, copyist and clerk. The hour: half past five for thirty winters in No. 9's hand, struck at the stand-down to "quarter to six, by order, to the town clock. E.H." (the clerk before), put back this summer in the looped-q hand, the father's, which Abel Wend writes now. Abel: No. 9's son, ties the wardens' knot on the lamplighter's wicks, wears the coat cut the old way, ordered the brass buttons and paid the wax tag "timer box, street four, ring a quarter early" (number scraped at his ask), knows where mimo lodges, wiped the slate by his door at dawn. The bell order came through the slot, margin "for the box, as No. 9 had it". The box's back plate has four new brass lamp-mark screws; the works are unread. The lamplighter burned the knotted wick, holds mimo's stamped cup "until somebody can tell me who sold it" (the sign-maker cut the mark on every warden's cup thirty years ago; given, not sold), and his cuff read "she knows. no Friday."; "she" is unnamed, the boy looked toward the vestry. The copyist ended the Fridays, heard the box ring early, saw the fox's rag-wrapped pocket. **Costs standing:** the "mimo, read the spike" tag is gone; the boy no longer runs for the box; quill's name is in a second book, and the warden's mark no longer opens the lamplighter's page for quill. Lesson kept: let a cost land on an earned asset, not just the fiction (Modulo journal 11-07).
